(a) In General.—In carrying out Phase 6.2 and Phase 6.2A of the Joint W78/88–1 Warhead Life Extension Program, the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Nuclear Weapons Council established by section 179 of title 10, United States Code, shall conduct a comparative analysis of the feasibility of, and preliminary design definitions and cost estimates for, each of the following life extension options:
        (1) A separate life extension option to produce a W78–1 warhead. 
        (2) A separate life extension option to produce a W88–1 warhead. 
        (3) An interoperable W78/88–1 life extension option. 
        (4) Any other life extension option the Nuclear Weapons Council considers appropriate.  
    (b) Limitation on Use of Funds.—None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act may be obligated or expended for Phase 6.3 (development engineering) activities for the Joint W78/88–1 Warhead Life Extension Program until the date that is 90 days after the Chairman of the Nuclear Weapons Council submits to the congressional defense committees a report containing the comparative analysis required by subsection (a).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the comparative analysis, the Nuclear Weapons Council, and the report requirement amount to a consultative process. Every actor is inside the federal government: the Secretaries of Defense and Energy, the Nuclear Weapons Council (a federal interagency body), and the congressional defense committees. Intra-government coordination and reports to Congress are not participation, and no outside party, public comment, rulemaking, or right to sue is involved.
fable.s: submits to the congressional defense committees a report containing the comparative analysis required by subsection (a)

qwen_block.w: The section requires federal officials (Secretaries of Defense and Energy) acting through a federal council (Nuclear Weapons Council) to conduct an analysis. It does not require consultation with or participation from any entities outside the federal government. The subsequent report is submitted to Congress, which is also inside the federal government. Therefore, no outside participation is involved.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Nuclear Weapons Council established by section 179 of title 10, United States Code, shall conduct a comparative analysis

opus.w: Everyone involved is inside the federal government: the Secretaries of Defense and Energy, the Nuclear Weapons Council, and the congressional defense committees. No states, experts, companies or members of the public are consulted, and there is no comment period, hearing or right to sue. The report-to-Congress condition looks procedural, but it never crosses the federal boundary, so it is not participation.
opus.s: until the date that is 90 days after the Chairman of the Nuclear Weapons Council submits to the congressional defense committees a report containing the comparative analysis required by subsection (a).
opus.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: the funding limit depends on a report to the congressional defense committees, which looks like a formal procedural check on the decision. That fails the definition because Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. The comparative analysis is also done entirely by federal officials: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Nuclear Weapons Council.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy to act through the Nuclear Weapons Council, which is an internal federal advisory body composed of government officials. The subsequent report is submitted to congressional defense committees, which are also part of the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies) before making the decision.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Energy, acting through the Nuclear Weapons Council established by section 179 of title 10, United States Code, shall conduct a comparative analysis
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Nuclear Weapons Council" involves outside experts or that the report to Congress constitutes participation. However, the Nuclear Weapons Council is an internal federal body (composed of senior military and civilian officials from DoD and DOE), and Congress is part of the federal government. Therefore, interactions with them are intra-governmental.
